headline_marked: South Africa's [[Navi Pillay wins Nobel Peace Prize]] for human rights work
headline: South Africa's Navi Pillay wins Nobel Peace Prize for human rights work
summary: The human rights champion, who led the Rwanda genocide tribunal, was honored for her efforts in prosecuting war crimes and crimes against humanity.
details: South Africa's Navi Pillay has been awarded the Nobel Peace Prize on Friday. The prize committee in Oslo highlighted her lifelong commitment to human rights and international law.
The Norwegian Nobel Committee chair, Jorgen Watne Frydnes, stated that Pillay has been instrumental in ensuring that genocide, war crimes, and crimes against humanity are prosecuted.
Pillay's career includes heading the Rwanda genocide tribunal, a critical role in seeking justice for victims of mass atrocities.
Last year, she gained further attention for accusing Israel of genocide in Gaza, continuing her advocacy for international legal accountability.
The United Nations described the award as a testament to the need and value of human rights in the current global climate.
Shabia Mantoo, a spokesperson for the UN human rights agency, called the award 'wonderful' and emphasized the importance of human rights more than ever.
caption:
A champion for justice and accountability. South Africa's Navi Pillay has won the Nobel Peace Prize.

South Africa's Navi Pillay has been awarded the Nobel Peace Prize on Friday. The prize committee in Oslo highlighted her lifelong commitment to human rights and international law.

The Norwegian Nobel Committee chair, Jorgen Watne Frydnes, stated that Pillay has been instrumental in ensuring that genocide, war crimes, and crimes against humanity are prosecuted.

Pillay's career includes heading the Rwanda genocide tribunal, a critical role in seeking justice for victims of mass atrocities.

Last year, she gained further attention for accusing Israel of genocide in Gaza, continuing her advocacy for international legal accountability.

The United Nations described the award as a testament to the need and value of human rights in the current global climate.

Shabia Mantoo, a spokesperson for the UN human rights agency, called the award 'wonderful' and emphasized the importance of human rights more than ever.

headline: CNG driver arrested for murder of class 7 student in Cumilla
summary: Police arrested the main accused, Sumon, in Chattogram after recovering an abandoned auto-rickshaw near the victim's body.
details: Police have arrested a CNG-run auto-rickshaw driver named Sumon in connection with the murder of Jannatul Tazmin, a class 7 student in Lalmai, Cumilla.
The suspect was apprehended from his brother's house in Chattogram. He is a resident of Joynagar in Lalmai and previously lived with his in-laws.
The investigation began after police recovered an abandoned CNG auto-rickshaw and a bag near where Tazmin's body was found in a paddy field in Jagatpur village.
Tazmin, a student at Farida Bidyayatan, had gone missing four days before her body was found. She had reportedly visited Cox's Bazar and was returning home when she got off near Paduar Bazar.
Police have also detained the vehicle's owner, Abul Hashem, and the suspect's aunt-in-law and brother-in-law for questioning.
The victim's father has filed a murder case with the Lalmai Police Station against unidentified individuals.
caption:
A CNG driver has been arrested in Chattogram for the murder of a class 7 student in Cumilla.

Police have arrested a CNG-run auto-rickshaw driver named Sumon in connection with the murder of Jannatul Tazmin, a class 7 student in Lalmai, Cumilla.

The suspect was apprehended from his brother's house in Chattogram. He is a resident of Joynagar in Lalmai and previously lived with his in-laws.

The investigation began after police recovered an abandoned CNG auto-rickshaw and a bag near where Tazmin's body was found in a paddy field in Jagatpur village.

Tazmin, a student at Farida Bidyayatan, had gone missing four days before her body was found. She had reportedly visited Cox's Bazar and was returning home when she got off near Paduar Bazar.

Police have also detained the vehicle's owner, Abul Hashem, and the suspect's aunt-in-law and brother-in-law for questioning.

The victim's father has filed a murder case with the Lalmai Police Station against unidentified individuals.
